<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_docs.py from the scixplorer source. Do not edit: run `uv run python scripts/gen_docs.py`. -->

Reference data held locally: journals, affiliations and two controlled vocabularies.

Each dataset is read from the user's cache if `refresh` has downloaded it, otherwise from the snapshot packaged with this library (journals and affiliations only). The Unified Astronomy Thesaurus and the planetary nomenclature gazetteer are not packaged: run `refresh("uat")` or `refresh("planetary_features")` once to use them.

Nothing is downloaded implicitly. `refresh` uses a plain HTTP client that never sends the SciX API token, because the sources are third-party hosts. Downloads are checked by the same parser the model uses before they replace the data in use, and are written atomically.

The packaged data files are not covered by this package's MIT licence: the affiliation files are GPL-3.0. `notices` returns the details.

The cache directory is `$SCIX_CACHE_DIR` if set, else `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/scixplorer`, else `~/Library/Caches/scixplorer` on macOS and `~/.cache/scixplorer` elsewhere.

## scixplorer.data.refresh

Written `scix.data.refresh` after `import scixplorer as scix`.

```python
refresh(*names, transport=None, timeout=60.0)
```

Download datasets into the cache, replacing the copies in use if the downloads are good.

With no names, every dataset with a public source is refreshed. Each download is parsed by its model before anything is written, and rejected (leaving the data in use untouched) if it does not parse, is empty, or has fewer than half as many records as the data in use. A dataset's files are replaced together or not at all. One dataset failing does not stop the others: check `ok` on each result.

Requests carry only a generic User-Agent; the SciX API token is never sent.

**Parameters**

- `transport`: an `httpx` transport, e.g. for testing or a proxy setup.
- `timeout`: seconds allowed for each request.

## scixplorer.data.status

Written `scix.data.status` after `import scixplorer as scix`.

```python
status()
```

Which copy of each dataset is in use, where it is, when it was modified and its size.

## scixplorer.data.clear

Written `scix.data.clear` after `import scixplorer as scix`.

```python
clear(*names)
```

Delete the cached copies of datasets (all if no names); packaged snapshots are kept.

Models then read their packaged snapshot, or raise `scix.exceptions.DataNotAvailable` if there is none.

## scixplorer.data.notices

Written `scix.data.notices` after `import scixplorer as scix`.

```python
notices()
```

The licence notice for the data files packaged with this library (`NOTICE.md`).

It says where each file comes from and under which licence; the packaged data is not covered by the package's MIT licence. The GPL-3.0 text it refers to is the package resource `LICENSE-GPL-3.0.txt` beside it.

## scixplorer.data.cache_dir

Written `scix.data.cache_dir` after `import scixplorer as scix`.

```python
cache_dir()
```

The directory holding downloaded data. It is created only when something is written.

## scixplorer.data.read_text

Written `scix.data.read_text` after `import scixplorer as scix`.

```python
read_text(dataset, filename)
```

The text of one file of a dataset: the cached copy if every file of the dataset is cached (as `load` and `status` decide), else the packaged one.

Raises `scix.exceptions.DataNotAvailable` if neither exists. The text is not checked; `load` checks it and falls back if it is bad.

## scixplorer.data.RefreshResult

Written `scix.data.RefreshResult` after `import scixplorer as scix`.

```python
RefreshResult(name, ok, files, message)
```

*class*

The outcome of refreshing one dataset. `files` are the cache files written.

## scixplorer.data.DatasetStatus

Written `scix.data.DatasetStatus` after `import scixplorer as scix`.

```python
DatasetStatus(name, source, paths, modified, size)
```

*class*

Which copy of a dataset is in use.

`source` is `"cache"` (downloaded by `refresh`), `"packaged"` or `"missing"`. `modified` (UTC) and `size` (bytes) cover all the files in `paths`; they are `None` when nothing can be inspected. The cached files are not parsed here, so an unreadable cache still shows as `"cache"` (the models then fall back to the packaged snapshot, with a `scix.exceptions.DataWarning`).

## scixplorer.data.Dataset

Written `scix.data.Dataset` after `import scixplorer as scix`.

```python
Dataset(name, files, packaged, licence, description)
```

*class*

A collection of reference data and where it comes from.

`files` is empty if there is no public source to refresh it from. `packaged` says whether a snapshot ships with this library. `licence` is the data's licence, as `notices` states it.

## scixplorer.data.RemoteFile

Written `scix.data.RemoteFile` after `import scixplorer as scix`.

```python
RemoteFile(url, filename, convert=None)
```

*class*

One file of a dataset: where it is published and its name in the cache.

The cached file always has the packaged format. `convert`, if given, turns the published text into that format.

### scixplorer.data.DATASETS

The datasets, by name: a read-only mapping of `Dataset`.

| Name | Packaged | Licence | Downloaded from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `journals` | yes | No licence stated (ADS bibliographic code list) | <https://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs_doc/journals.html> |
| `affiliations` | yes | GPL-3.0 (adsabs/CanonicalAffiliations) | <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adsabs/CanonicalAffiliations/master/parent_child.tsv><br><https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adsabs/CanonicalAffiliations/master/country_parent_child.tsv> |
| `uat` | no | CC BY-SA 3.0 (American Astronomical Society) | <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astrothesaurus/UAT/master/UAT_list.json> |
| `planetary_features` | no | Public domain (USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature), via an MIT-licensed adsabs repository | <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adsabs/ADSPlanetaryNamesPipeline/main/docs/Gazetteer_of_Planetary_Nomenclature_Exported_Nov_7_2024.csv> |

## For model authors

Models use these to read their data; you do not need them to use scixplorer.

### scixplorer.data.register

Written `scix.data.register` after `import scixplorer as scix`.

```python
register(name, parse, reset)
```

Register how a model reads dataset `name`; models call this when imported.

**Parameters**

- `parse`: builds the model's records from a `Reader`; it raises on malformed data. `load` and `refresh` both use it.
- `reset`: forgets everything the model has cached from the data, so the next query reads it again. Called after `refresh` or `clear`.

### scixplorer.data.load

Written `scix.data.load` after `import scixplorer as scix`.

```python
load(name, parse)
```

Parse dataset `name` with `parse`: the cached copy if usable, else the packaged one.

An unusable cached copy is skipped with a `scix.exceptions.DataWarning`. Raises `scix.exceptions.DataNotAvailable` if there is no usable copy and nothing is packaged.
